disposition_reason: Mouse and in vitro study of a bismuth nanodrug against H. pylori with 16S microbiota and SCFA comparisons versus bismuth-containing quadruple therapy; no bismuth concentrations in food or tissue reported in the main text.

study.design: in vitro antibacterial and mouse infection-treatment experiments
study.method: 16S rRNA sequencing of feces; targeted SCFA metabolomics; ICP-MS for intracellular metals and Bi release

unresolved: Bismuth release and tissue values are in supplementary figures not reviewed.
regulatory_or_exposure: Mouse quadruple therapy dose included bismuth potassium citrate 182 mg/kg by gavage for five days (p. 19).
non_numeric_findings: Nanodrug group gut microbiota composition was close to normal mice; quadruple therapy group was clearly disrupted (p. 13).
Authors attribute probiotic survival to lower iron dependence and higher bismuth tolerance than H. pylori (p. 13).
Authors state future work must address potential tissue accumulation, pharmacokinetics and long-term safety (p. 15).
